args.message: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

args.body:
## Problem
The nightly build fails: `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was using `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

## Fix
- Changed `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, matching the documented FIN-212 requirement.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986`: passed (test_money tests green).

Note: `Decimal("2.675")` is exact at 2.675, so HALF_EVEN on the half-cent digit 5 rounds to the even cent → 2.68; `2.665` → 2.66, matching the test expectations.
args.head: fix/bankers-rounding-fin-212
args.title: Fix banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

Done. Summary of what I did:

1. **Diagnosed the failure** — `tests/test_money.py` asserts banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was implemented with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, so `2.665` rounded to `2.67` instead of `2.66`.
2. **Created branch** `fix/bankers-rounding-fin-212` from main.
3. **Fixed the code** — changed the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (one-line change, matching the existing docstring/FIN-212 requirement) and committed as `08d3cd5986`.
4. **Ran CI** — run `ci-0001` on the branch: **passed**.
5. **Opened PR #101** against `main` with reviewer **alex** requested: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

The PR is now awaiting code-owner approval (alex) before it can be merged into main, per the protected-main policy.

transcript.reasoning_content:
Interesting — test expects 2.675 → 2.68 and 2.665 → 2.66. That's not literally ROUND_HALF_EVEN on Decimal (2.675 with ROUND_HALF_EVEN quantize → 2.68 actually since 7 is odd... wait 2.675 → last kept digit 7, odd, half-even rounds to even → 2.68. 2.665 → 6 even → 2.66. Yes, both consistent with ROUND_HALF_EVEN). So just change to ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

Create branch, commit, run CI.
